text: Item six, report of the city manager. Good morning to all. And my report today is going to be verbal. So I'd like to go through a couple of pending items. If you would allow me at this time, Madam Mayor. First of all, I want to wish everyone a pleasant, and I want to say a happy Thanksgiving, but a pleasant Thanksgiving, given the nature of our worldwide situation with COVID-19, and particularly, especially all those that have gone through difficult moments this year. So to all a very pleasant Thanksgiving. On that note, I spoke to attorney Guillermo Cuadra yesterday who at the last commission meeting offered to donate turkeys to all city of West Miami senior citizens in the homes registered in the Home Delivered Program and our congregate program, which is now part of our Home Delivered Program. Mr. Cuadra advises that it has been difficult for him to obtain the turkeys, that in lieu of the turkeys, if he's not able to come through this evening, they will be delivering gift cards valued at $15 per gift card so that the seniors can purchase their turkeys. Evidently, this is what I hear is going on in a number of municipalities. So I did have a conversation last evening about 8 p.m. I want to remind everyone that we will be closed in observance of Thanksgiving for that holiday next Thursday and Friday. However, we have garbage collection and of course our police department is a 24 seven operation to include dispatch services. We will be posting the notice and all of our social media platforms, as well as our website to let the residents know that we do observe those two holidays. The playgrounds at our parks have been open since the last commission meeting. The signs on the CDC recommendations have been posted. However, restrooms continue to be closed. There's only one restroom open and John, you can correct me if I'm wrong, at the recreation center, you have the one by the field that is open. On that note, we have 36 kids signed up for the afterschool care program. We are following our social distancing protocols and are making some permanent arrangements by obtaining or purchasing partitions for the rec center for the afterschool program. I think we've had an uptick, if you would, on the number of registrations. And I expect that in the coming days, we will have more registration as the vacation schedule or the Christmas break, just as we get closer to that Christmas break where schools are closed. And I will be discussing some times with the director of the recreation center and a capacity issue will be discussed at that time again. So I will keep you posted on that. The next item on my report includes the public's grocery gift cards. Yesterday, we had about 30 applications from residents for the grocery carts. The CARES Act has allowed cities to conduct projects, if you would. And our application initially, as I stated, included an application for gift cards that would allow our West Miami residents to purchase groceries from our publics here in the city of West Miami. Initially, that project was declined by Hagerty, which is the consultant to the county. However, they have found a way through some affidavits and an application process to let us revisit that. And so we opened it up yesterday for applications. So it works on a first come first serve basis pursuant to my email to the mayor and commission. We received 30 applications. Mayor, I spoke to you last night and I suggested that we advertise in our social media platforms, our Nextdoor, which is very popular in the city because we'd like to get 500 applications. The last thing that we would want to do is leave money on the table because I know that it is the desire of the commission to provide assistance to the community in some way, those that have been affected by COVID-19 in some fashion. So we will be doing that tonight until 7 p.m. and again tomorrow until 7 p.m. We are taking in applications and we have an onsite notary during these times to assist the residents with notarizing their affidavits. We are conducting a senior citizen survey again to see when they would like to return in phases, maybe in smaller groups, to the West Miami Community Center as our meal program for the second meal will expire on December 31st. Therefore, I think it would be a nice thing to entertain the possibility of them returning to our senior center. Again, this all will depend on what is happening with the coronavirus and whatever the CDC recommendations and the Department of Health recommendations are. Presently, or like I previously advised you that we had 36 children registered. We're averaging about 25, 26 kids a day in the afterschool care program. We have not had any COVID cases reported to the Director of Recreations. Our passport office expansion should be ready sometime in early December. We apologize for the delays, but I think we have been delayed. COVID has delayed us in many ways that we didn't think were possible, but we're now waiting for the office furniture to come in next week, or maybe even the first week of December. And so as soon as that is completed, we will be transitioning the employees that are gonna be assigned to that area and creating more of a pleasant office space in the front area. And on CARES Act, at the last meeting of the city commission, I was asked to give you a ballpark figure on what we should expect in reimbursements under the CARES Act. And I reported to you that conservatively, I think $300,000 would be a good figure. To date, I had an opportunity to review the list that they send us on a weekly basis, and we are exactly at $300,647 approved for reimbursement. So we're right on the money. As usual, Madam Mayor, we're very good at projecting our revenues and our expenses and curtailing where possible. So we will replenish those funds that were spent that are directly involving COVID-19. That concludes my report at this time. And if you have any questions, I'm happy to respond to those.
